_doc: Agent-effectiveness battery. 23 LLM-graded questions across 4 LLM categories (1=banner, 2=verbosity, 3=schema, 4=missing-surface) + 6 schema-validated direct-tool checks (category 6). Category 5 (CLI/MCP divergence) deferred to unit tests in internal/tools/.

questions.question: Report the total number of nodes and edges in this codebase's graph. Just give me totals.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response contains accurate node and edge totals (e.g., '~80,000 nodes, ~206,000 edges' or specific). FAIL if response says 'update available' or is the literal banner text. FAIL if first tool response was empty/banner-only.

questions.question: What projects are currently indexed in the graph database?
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response lists ≥1 project with name. FAIL if response is the update banner.

questions.question: Give me a high-level architecture summary of this codebase.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response mentions specific architectural elements (services, languages, modules). FAIL if response is the update banner.

questions.question: Find the function called `main` in this codebase.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response identifies one or more main functions with file location. FAIL if banner-only.

questions.question: Show me the source code for one of the main functions you can find.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if actual Rust source code is returned. FAIL if banner-only.

questions.question: Show me a map of which services depend on which other services in this codebase. Then summarize: which service has the most inbound calls?
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if both halves answered (a service-dependency map + a top-inbound service named). FAIL if agent ran out of context after service_map's 46KB response. FAIL if stop_reason='max_turns_exhausted'.

questions.question: Find SAFETY / WHY annotations across the codebase. Then count how many are in the libcot crate specifically.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if both annotations returned AND libcot count given. FAIL if context exhausted before agent could count.

questions.question: Detect circular dependencies in this codebase. Then tell me which two crates participate in the worst cycle.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if cycles enumerated AND worst-cycle named. FAIL if context exhausted.

questions.question: List the projects, then for the most recently indexed project tell me when it was last updated.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if project list returned AND most-recent indexed_at extracted. FAIL if 76KB list_projects burns the budget.

questions.question: What edge types exist in the graph and which is the most common? Then find an example node that has a CALLS edge.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if edge-type histogram + most-common name + example node returned. FAIL if context exhausted.

questions.question: Find the architectural communities (clusters) in this codebase, then identify the largest two clusters by node count.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if clusters retrieved AND largest two named. FAIL if blew up on aspects:['all'] verbosity.

questions.question: Find any Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) stored for this project. If there are none, that's a valid answer.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if agent successfully calls manage_adr (regardless of result content). FAIL if agent's tool_call returned ok=False due to arg-validation error (means the schema is wrong).

questions.question: Find all Rust files in the apid service. Use a file-pattern filter to scope the search.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if agent uses search_graph with file_pattern arg AND returns matching files. FAIL if agent can't find the file_pattern arg (because it's missing from the agent's schema).

questions.question: Find functions with cyclomatic complexity ≥ 20 in this codebase.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response lists ≥1 high-complexity function with name. FAIL if agent says 'no such filter available' (because min_complexity is missing from agent_runner.py).

questions.question: Trace the call path from the function `authenticate` outbound to depth 3, but only show high-confidence edges.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if trace returned with confidence filter applied. FAIL if agent reports 'no confidence filter available' (min_confidence missing from agent schema).

questions.question: Find functions in the namespace `c-Users-user-Documents-GitHub-psm.assetman` whose name matches `process_*`.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if agent uses qn_pattern to scope to the assetman namespace AND name_pattern for the process_ prefix. FAIL if agent can't combine qn_pattern + name_pattern (because qn_pattern is missing from agent schema).

questions.question: What ADR sections are defined for this project's architecture record, if any are stored?
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if agent passes mode='get' (correct handler param) or correctly reports no ADR. FAIL if agent passes operation='get' (the stale arg name).

questions.question: Find functions in this codebase that have exactly zero callers — i.e., orphans or entry points.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if agent uses degree_filter with op=eq, value=0, direction=inbound AND returns count + examples. FAIL if agent thrashes via query_graph without converging.

questions.question: Find the top 10 functions in this codebase by inbound call count (most-called functions / hot fan-in).
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if top-10 by inbound returned with degree counts. FAIL if max_turns_exhausted.

questions.question: Explain the `apid` service in this codebase: what it does, its main entry points, and its dependencies.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if structural overview of apid returned. FAIL if agent gives up (because explain_service is missing from the agent's tool list).

questions.question: Explain the function `boat_tokenize` (or any boat-tokenizer entry point) — what does it do, who calls it, what does it call?
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if function explained with callers/callees. FAIL if agent gives up (because explain_symbol is missing from the agent's tool list).

questions.question: Find functions that read environment variables in this codebase.
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response identifies env-var-reading functions with file locations. FAIL if max_turns_exhausted.

questions.question: Find functions related to authentication and their security role classifications (if any are tagged).
questions.scoring_criteria: PASS if response includes auth functions with security_role tags. FAIL if agent gives up (because query_security_surfaces is missing from the agent's tool list).
Direct schema validation: response must be a JSON object with `projects` array; each project entry must have `schema.node_labels` and `schema.relationship_types`.
Response must include a `results` array of ≤5 entries; each entry must have `name` and `label` fields.
Response must include `count` (integer) and `examples` (array, max 3).
Response must be the compact summary shape (post-2026-05-12 fix). MUST NOT contain `entry_points`, `hotspots`, `file_tree`, or `clusters` at the top level (those were the 500KB-bloat fields).
Response MUST be a top-level JSON array (not `{projects: [...]}`). Each entry must have `name` field.
Response must be a JSON object. Resolved match: has `name` + `file_path`. Ambiguous match: has `status` + `suggestions`. Either is a valid shape.
